metadata.note: The two railroads that gave Santa Rosa, CA its passenger rail service, researched from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites in response to a question about whether Santa Rosa had passenger rail in 1934 -- it did (mainline Northwestern Pacific trains), and this dataset had no coverage of the North Bay at all before. The Northwestern Pacific Railroad traces back to the San Francisco and North Pacific Railroad, whose first train reached Santa Rosa from Petaluma Oct 22 1870; seven North Coast railroads consolidated into the Northwestern Pacific in 1907 (jointly owned by the Southern Pacific and Santa Fe), completing a through San Francisco Bay-Eureka route by 1915 and running Santa Rosa passenger trains until 1958. Separately, the Petaluma and Santa Rosa Railway was an electric interurban (1904-1932) that gave Santa Rosa a second, cheaper rail option via Sebastopol -- including a colorful 1905 confrontation, the 'Battle of Sebastopol Avenue,' when it had to cross the steam-powered California Northwestern's tracks to reach downtown Santa Rosa. The Northwestern Pacific itself bought the P&SR in 1932 and ended its trolley service, two years before the year asked about, leaving the NWP's own mainline as Santa Rosa's only passenger rail from 1932 to 1958. GEOMETRY UPDATE: the Northwestern Pacific route is no longer a 9-waypoint sketch - it is now traced from real track via OSM (Overpass + shortest-path search), 275 points over 272 miles, which matches the 271-mile mainline figure Wikipedia gives and follows the Eel River Canyon properly instead of cutting Willits-Eureka as one straight line. The Petaluma and Santa Rosa interurban is still a 3-waypoint sketch. The NWP is now split into three features so the slider shows the line reaching Eureka only from 1914: the south end (1870-1914), the completed through route (1914-1958), and the Willits-Eureka Budd car that outlived it (1958-1971). CAVEAT ON THE NAME: through passenger trains to Eureka actually ran from SAUSALITO, and from San Rafael by the 1950s - Tiburon was a separate terminal on the same railroad (trains #133 Santa Rosa-Tiburon, #4 Tiburon-San Rafael, #109 Tiburon-Sausalito) and lost its trains in 1967. The Tiburon end is kept here because that is how this dataset already modelled the line; the Sausalito branch is not yet mapped. Era boundaries follow real corporate-history milestones (line openings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not sourced from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Northwestern Pacific Railroad, San Francisco and North Pacific Railroad, Petaluma and Santa Rosa Railroad), cmosc.org, pressdemocrat.com, santarosahistory.com, noehill.com (see conversation for citations)
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.
metadata.psr_feature_moved: 2026-09-30: feature psr-petaluma-santa-rosa (the Petaluma and Santa Rosa interurban, a 3-point straight-line sketch dated 1904-1932) was removed from this file and replaced by petaluma_and_santa_rosa_railroad.geojson, which traces the line in five features (Petaluma-Sebastopol, Sebastopol-Santa Rosa, Fourth Street in Santa Rosa, Sebastopol-Forestville, Two Rock Branch) in its own colour #B5838D. The old feature carried the Northwestern Pacific's #386641, a Rule 4 error: the P&SR ran its own trains until passenger service ended on Jun 30 1932, and the NWP only acquired its stock on Feb 26 1932. The P&SR sentences in this file's note above describe the removed sketch and are kept as history.

NOTE: this feature draws the south end at its eventual full extent; the individual pieces (including the Tiburon terminal, opened 1884) were assembled progressively, so the early years overstate how much of it existed.

Douglas-Peucker simplified to ~150 m. Replaces the earlier 9-waypoint sketch.

segments.note: The Willits-Eureka gap through the Eel River Canyon was closed with a golden spike ceremony in October 1914, completing the through route. All mainline passenger service south of Willits was discontinued on November 10, 1958, per Wikipedia. NOTE: through passenger trains actually ran from Sausalito, not Tiburon - see the layer metadata.

segments.note: After November 10, 1958 the only NWP passenger service left was a tri-weekly Willits-Eureka round trip run by a single Budd Rail Diesel Car. It ran until April 30, 1971; Amtrak did not continue service on the NWP, per Wikipedia.
